The study used trilayer heterostructures with varying Mg doping levels.
The thickness of the (Ga,Mn)N layer was between 3.8 and 4.8 nm.
The Mn concentration in the middle of the layer did not exceed 5%.
The Mg doping level in the cladding GaN:Mg layers varied from 3×10^17 cm^-3 to 9×10^20 cm^-3.
The neighboring GAN:Mg layers had no effect on the spin-spin interactions in the central (Ga,Mn)N layer.
The layers exhibited purely paramagnetic response above 50 K.
The study used HRTEM, EDX, and SIMS for structural characterization.
The dedicated experimental approach was used for in situ compensation of the magnetic contribution from the substrate.
The precision of the magnetometer was 5×10^-7 emu at 70 kOe.
The study found no effect of the Mg doping on the magnetic properties of the (Ga,Mn)N layer.
The (Ga,Mn)N layer was sandwiched between two thicker GaN:Mg cladding layers.
The study used molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) for growth of the trilayer heterostructures.
The Ga flux was 2×10^-6 Torr BEP.
The Mn flux was 1×10^-6 Torr BEP.
The Mg flux varied from 0 to 2×10^-8 Torr BEP.
